what_they_do: Nebula builds a memory infrastructure layer that developers plug into AI agents so the agents can retain and recall context over time. It ingests documents, conversations, files, and connected sources (Slack, Gmail, Notion, Google Drive), then structures that raw content into entities, facts, and source utterances with contradiction detection and confidence scoring, replacing the manual work of stuffing flat conversation history or ad hoc context files into a model's prompt. Nebula is the first product from Zeroset, an applied AI research lab; the product is also distributed as a memory plugin for the OpenClaw agent framework.
theme_fit_rationale: Nebula is horizontal infrastructure built specifically for AI agents as the end user, not a human-facing app: API/SDK-first (Python, JS, REST, MCP), sold to developers deploying production agents, solving a machine-native problem (state retention across sessions) rather than a human workflow. This matches Theme 3's thesis that every software category gets rebuilt around machine-readable interfaces for non-human users, with memory/context being one of the underlying primitives agents need alongside identity, communication, and observability.
